Asus ROG Phone 6 Diablo Immortal Edition

generated_text_by_instance.text: The Parla Sonic 3.5 is a discontinued entry-level Dual SIM smartphone released in late 2013. It features a compact 3.5-inch TFT display (320x480), runs Android 4.1 (Jelly Bean) on a Spreadtrum SC7710G chipset, and has minimal memory with 512MB of RAM. Key hardware includes a 2MP main camera, a removable 1300 mAh battery, and basic connectivity including Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 2.1, though it lacks a selfie camera and GPS.

The Karbonn Titanium Hexa is a discontinued Android 4.4.2 smartphone released in April 2014. It features a 5.5-inch Full HD IPS LCD display, a hexa-core 1.5 GHz CPU, 2GB of RAM, and 16GB of internal storage. For photography, it includes a 13MP main camera and a 5MP selfie camera, all powered by a 2050 mAh Li-Po battery.

The QMobile E1 is a discontinued Android 6.0 smartphone released in January 2017. It features a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display (720x1280), a Mediatek MT6735P quad-core processor, 3GB of RAM, and 16GB of internal storage. Notable hardware includes an 8MP main camera, a 5MP selfie camera, and a large 4000mAh removable Li-Po battery.

The Garmin-Asus nuvifone A50 is a discontinued Android 2.1 smartphone released in 2010. It features a 3.5-inch TFT display, a Qualcomm Snapdragon S1 processor (600 MHz), 256MB RAM, and 4GB of internal storage. Notable for its Garmin navigation capabilities, it includes a 3.15 MP main camera, but lacks a selfie camera and a 3.5mm headphone jack. It is powered by a removable 1150 mAh battery.

Released in May 2023, the Infinix Note 30 5G is a budget-friendly smartphone featuring a 6.78-inch 120Hz IPS LCD display and a Mediatek Dimensity 6080 chipset. It boasts a high-resolution 108MP triple main camera, a 16MP selfie camera, and is powered by a 5000mAh battery with 45W fast charging. Available in configurations up to 8GB RAM and 256GB storage, it also includes JBL-tuned dual speakers and NFC support.

The Asus ROG Phone 6 Diablo Immortal Edition is a high-performance gaming smartphone released in November 2022. It features a 6.78-inch 165Hz AMOLED display, a Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 chipset, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of internal storage. Designed for gamers, it includes pressure-sensitive triggers, an illuminated RGB logo, a large 6000mAh battery with 65W fast charging, and dual USB-C ports. The device is equipped with a 50MP triple main camera system capable of 8K video and is finished in 'Hellfire Red'.

The Samsung Galaxy F34, released in August 2023, is a 5G-enabled smartphone featuring a 6.5-inch Super AMOLED 120Hz display and a massive 6000mAh battery with 25W wired charging. It is powered by the Exynos 1280 chipset with 128GB storage and options for 6GB or 8GB of RAM. Notable hardware includes a triple main camera setup led by a 50MP OIS sensor, a 13MP selfie camera, and Gorilla Glass 5 protection, priced at approximately 210 EUR.

The Micromax In 2b, released in August 2021, is an affordable Android 11 smartphone priced around 90 EUR. It features a 6.52-inch IPS LCD display, a Unisoc T610 octa-core chipset, and 64GB of storage with either 4GB or 6GB of RAM. Notable hardware includes a 5000 mAh battery with 10W charging, a 13MP dual rear camera, and a 5MP selfie camera.

The Philips S396 is a discontinued dual-SIM smartphone released in June 2015. It features a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display (720x1280), runs Android 5.1 Lollipop, and is powered by a Mediatek MT6735P quad-core processor with 1GB RAM and 8GB internal storage. It is equipped with 8MP front and rear cameras, LTE connectivity, and a removable 2300 mAh battery.

The Prestigio MultiPhone 7600 Duo is a discontinued Dual SIM Android 4.2 smartphone released in Q1 2014. It features a large 6.0-inch IPS LCD display (720x1280), a quad-core 1.5 GHz CPU, and basic memory with 1GB RAM and 4GB internal storage. For photography, it is equipped with a 13MP main camera and an 8MP selfie camera. It is powered by a removable 2600 mAh battery and was priced at approximately 270 EUR.

The Cubot Tab KingKong is a rugged Android 13 tablet released in August 2023, featuring IP68/IP69K dust and water resistance. It boasts a 10.1-inch IPS LCD (1200x1920), a Mediatek MT8788 chipset, 8GB RAM, and 256GB of internal storage. Notable for its endurance, it includes a large 10,600 mAh battery with 18W wired charging, a 16MP main camera, and LTE connectivity.

Released in September 2023, the Honor V Purse is a 5G foldable smartphone featuring a 7.71-inch 90Hz OLED main display and a 6.45-inch cover display, both with 1600 nits peak brightness. It is powered by a Snapdragon 778G 5G chipset, 16GB of RAM, and storage options of 256GB or 512GB. The device includes a 50MP dual main camera system, a 4500 mAh battery with 35W wired charging, and runs Android 13. It is priced at approximately 770 EUR.

The Archos Oxygen 68XL is a budget-friendly Android 9.0 smartphone released in May 2019, priced around 150 EUR. It features a massive 6.85-inch IPS LCD display, a large 5000 mAh battery, and is powered by a Mediatek Helio P22 chipset with 3GB RAM and 32GB storage. It includes a dual rear camera (8MP main) and a 5MP selfie camera.

The O2 XDA Comet is a discontinued Windows Mobile 6.0 Professional smartphone released in September 2007. It features a 2.7-inch resistive touchscreen, an Intel XScale PXA 270 620 MHz CPU, 64MB RAM, and a 2MP main camera. Connectivity includes HSPA, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 1.2, and an infrared port, powered by a removable 1350mAh Li-Ion battery.

Released in October 2023, the Oppo A79 is a 5G-enabled smartphone featuring a 6.72-inch 90Hz IPS LCD display and a Mediatek Dimensity 6020 chipset. It comes with 8GB RAM, 128GB UFS 2.2 storage, and a 50MP dual main camera. The device is powered by a 5000 mAh battery with 33W fast charging and is IPX4 splash resistant.

The ZTE Blade A73 5G, released in September 2023, is an affordable 5G smartphone featuring a 6.52-inch 90Hz IPS LCD display and a Unisoc T760 chipset. It comes with 128GB storage, 4GB RAM, and a large 5000mAh battery. For photography, it sports a 50MP dual main camera and a 5MP selfie camera, running on Android 13.

The Sagem Puma Phone is a discontinued 2010 GSM/HSPA device tailored for fitness, featuring an integrated solar cell and dedicated bike, run, and pedometer trackers. It has a 2.8-inch resistive touchscreen, a 3.15 MP main camera, and a removable 880 mAh battery. Other notable specs include GPS, Bluetooth 2.1, and a 2 GB microSDHC card, originally priced around 400 EUR.

Released in November 2019, the Cat S52 is a rugged smartphone featuring IP68 water/dust resistance, MIL-STD-810G compliance, and drop-to-concrete resistance. It sports a 5.65-inch IPS LCD (720p) protected by Gorilla Glass 6, and is powered by a Mediatek Helio P35 chipset with 4GB RAM and 64GB storage. The device includes a 12MP main camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and a 3100 mAh battery, retailing for approximately 440 EUR.

The Oppo Reno11 (China), announced in November 2023, is a 5G smartphone featuring a 6.7-inch 120Hz OLED display and powered by the Mediatek Dimensity 8200 chipset on Android 14. It offers storage options up to 512GB with up to 12GB RAM, a triple rear camera system led by a 50MP main sensor with OIS, and a 32MP selfie camera. The device is equipped with a 4800 mAh battery supporting 67W fast charging and is priced at approximately 320 EUR.

Released in November 2018, the Panasonic P85 Nxt is an entry-level Dual SIM smartphone featuring a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display with Gorilla Glass protection. It is powered by a Snapdragon 210 quad-core processor, 2GB of RAM, and 16GB of internal storage, running Android 7.1.2. Notable features include a large 4000 mAh battery, a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor, an 8MP main camera, and a 5MP selfie camera. It was priced at approximately 7000 INR.

The BenQ-Siemens EF61 is a discontinued GSM phone released in July 2006. It features a compact 99g design with a primary 128x160 TFT display, a secondary external CSTN screen, and a 1.3MP main camera. Connectivity is limited to Bluetooth and USB 1.1, while memory is supported by a dedicated microSD slot and 1.5MB of internal storage. It is powered by a removable 750 mAh Li-Ion battery providing up to 3 hours of talk time.

The Alcatel 1B (2022) is an entry-level smartphone released in May 2022, priced around 100 EUR. It features a 5.5-inch TFT LCD display (720x1440), is powered by a Helio A22 quad-core chipset with 2GB RAM and 32GB storage, and runs Android 11 (Go edition). It includes an 8MP main camera, a 5MP selfie camera, and a removable 3000 mAh battery.

The T-Mobile Revvlry, released in July 2019, is an entry-level Android 9.0 smartphone featuring a 5.7-inch IPS LCD display (720p) and a Snapdragon 632 octa-core processor. It comes with 3GB of RAM, 32GB of internal storage (expandable via microSD), and a 3000 mAh battery with 10W charging. For photography, it includes a 13MP main camera and an 8MP selfie camera, both capable of 1080p video. Additional features include splash resistance, a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor, and a 3.5mm headphone jack, with a launch price of approximately 180 EUR.

Released in November 2023, the Honor X50i+ is a slim, lightweight 5G smartphone featuring a 6.7-inch 90Hz AMOLED display with a peak brightness of 2000 nits. It is powered by a Dimensity 6080 chipset, 12GB of RAM, and storage options of 256GB or 512GB. Notable hardware includes a 108MP main camera, a 4500mAh battery with 35W wired charging, and a side-mounted fingerprint sensor, priced at approximately 210 EUR.

Released in May 2019, the Vodafone Smart N10 is an entry-level Android 9.0 smartphone priced around 150 EUR. It features a 5.67-inch IPS LCD display, a Mediatek Helio A22 quad-core processor, and basic memory specs with 2GB RAM and 16GB internal storage. The device includes a 13MP main camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and is powered by a 2920 mAh battery.

Released in December 2021, the Philips PH1 is an affordable Android smartphone priced around 70 EUR. It features a 6.51-inch IPS LCD display, a Unisoc Tiger T310 quad-core chipset, 4GB of RAM, and storage options ranging from 32GB to 128GB. The device is equipped with a 13MP dual main camera, a 5MP selfie camera, and a 4700 mAh battery.

The Sony Ericsson Xperia active is a discontinued, rugged compact smartphone released in October 2011. It features a 3.0-inch display, IP67 dust/water resistance, and a built-in flashlight. Powered by a 1.0 GHz Snapdragon S2 processor and 512MB RAM, it originally ran Android 2.3 (upgradable to 4.0). Key hardware includes a 5MP main camera with 720p video, a removable 1200 mAh battery, and a microSDHC slot.

Released in February 2022, the Sharp Aquos V6 is a budget-friendly smartphone priced around 130 EUR. It features a 6.52-inch IPS LCD display, a Mediatek Helio G25 chipset with 3GB RAM and 32GB storage, and a large 5000 mAh battery with USB Power Delivery 3.0. The device includes a triple rear camera setup (13MP wide, 2MP macro, and 2MP depth) and a 5MP selfie camera, running on Android 12.

The OnePlus Nord CE 3 Lite, released in April 2023, is a budget-friendly 5G smartphone featuring a large 6.72-inch 120Hz IPS LCD display and a Snapdragon 695 5G chipset. It is equipped with 8GB of RAM and storage options of 128GB or 256GB. Notable highlights include a high-resolution 108MP main camera, a 5000mAh battery with fast 67W wired charging, and stereo speakers with a 3.5mm jack.

The Archos Oxygen 63 is a budget Android 9.0 smartphone released in May 2019, priced at approximately 130 EUR. It features a 6.26-inch IPS LCD display (720x1520), is powered by a Unisoc SC9863 octa-core chipset with 4GB RAM and 64GB storage, and includes a removable 3000 mAh battery. The device is equipped with a dual rear camera (8MP + 0.3MP), a 5MP selfie camera, and a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor.

The Parla Mist is a discontinued 2012 feature phone featuring a QWERTY keyboard, triple SIM support, and a small 1.8-inch TFT display. It is a basic GSM device with a VGA main camera, Bluetooth 2.1, and a removable 700 mAh battery, offering up to 6 hours of talk time.

Released in April 2019, the Allview Soul X6 Xtreme is an Android 9.0 smartphone featuring a 6.39-inch AMOLED display protected by Gorilla Glass 5 and an under-display fingerprint sensor. It is powered by a Mediatek Helio P70 octa-core chipset with 4GB RAM and 64GB storage. Notable features include a motorized pop-up 8MP selfie camera, a 16MP dual main camera, and a 3450 mAh battery supporting 18W wired and wireless charging.

The i-mobile Hitz 2206 is a discontinued dual-SIM GSM phone released in 2010. It features a QWERTY keyboard, a 220x176 pixel TFT display, a 0.3MP main camera, and a removable 1000 mAh battery. Connectivity is limited to GPRS and Stereo FM radio, with no support for Bluetooth, WLAN, or USB.

The Eten glofiish X900 is a discontinued Windows Mobile 6.1 Professional smartphone released in June 2008. It features a 2.8-inch resistive touchscreen (480 x 640 pixels), a Samsung 533 MHz CPU, 128MB RAM, and a 3.15 MP main camera. Connectivity includes HSPA, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 2.0, and GPS, powered by a removable 1300mAh Li-Ion battery.

Released in July 2022, the Yezz Max 2 Ultra is an entry-level Android 11 smartphone featuring a 6.1-inch IPS LCD display (600x1280) and a Mediatek MT6737M quad-core processor. It comes with 2GB of RAM, 32GB of internal storage, and a removable 3000 mAh battery. For photography, it offers a 13MP dual main camera and an 8MP selfie camera, and includes a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor.

The Tel.Me. T939 was a cancelled 2004 GSM phone running Windows PocketPC 2003. It featured a 160x240 resistive touchscreen, a 2MP autofocus camera with LED flash, an infrared port, and an 800mAh removable Li-Ion battery.

The LG K52, released in November 2020, is a budget-friendly Android 10 smartphone featuring a 6.6-inch IPS LCD display (720x1600) and a Mediatek Helio P35 chipset. It is equipped with 64GB storage, 4GB RAM, and a 4000mAh battery. Notable features include a quad-camera setup led by a 48MP main sensor, a 13MP selfie camera, MIL-STD-810G compliance, and a side-mounted fingerprint sensor.

The Wind DUO 2000 is a discontinued Dual SIM GSM phone announced in March 2007. It features a compact 1.5-inch OLED display, Bluetooth 1.2, and a removable 1660 mAh battery, but lacks a camera, WLAN, and a 3.5mm jack. Basic capabilities include an MP3 player, Java support, and WAP 2.0 browsing.

The Modu Sport jacket is a discontinued 2009 GSM device featuring a small 1.3-inch AMOLED display and 1.6GB of internal memory. Designed for activity, it includes a built-in pedometer, sport application, and MP3 player, powered by a removable 530 mAh battery. It lacks a camera, WLAN, and browser, relying on Bluetooth 1.2 for connectivity.

Released in September 2023, the Doogee T10Plus is an Android 13 tablet featuring a 10.5-inch IPS LCD display (1200 x 1920 pixels) with stylus support. It is powered by a Unisoc T606 octa-core chipset, 8GB of RAM, and 256GB of internal storage. The device includes a 13MP dual main camera, an 8MP selfie camera, quad stereo speakers, and a large 8250 mAh battery with 18W wired charging. It is built with an aluminum frame and back, weighing 505g.

The Sony Ericsson Xperia mini pro is a discontinued compact Android smartphone released in August 2011. It features a 3.0-inch LCD display, a physical QWERTY keyboard, and is powered by a 1.0 GHz Snapdragon S2 processor with 512MB RAM. The device includes a 5MP main camera capable of 720p video, a VGA selfie camera, and is powered by a removable 1200 mAh battery.

The Nvidia Shield is a discontinued 8.0-inch Android tablet released in July 2014. It features a 1920 x 1200 IPS LCD display, is powered by an Nvidia Tegra K1 chipset with a quad-core 2.2 GHz CPU, and includes 2GB of RAM and 16GB of internal storage. Notable hardware includes a stylus, HDMI port, stereo speakers with dual bass reflex ports, and a 5400 mAh battery.

Released in September 2023, the Doogee S41 Pro is a rugged Android 12 smartphone featuring MIL-STD-810H compliance, IP68/IP69K water and dust resistance, and drop protection up to 1.8m. It is powered by a Helio A22 chipset with 4GB RAM and 64GB storage, supported by a massive 6300 mAh battery. The device has a 5.5-inch IPS LCD (720p), a 13MP triple main camera, and an 8MP selfie camera.

The Posh Volt Max LTE L640 is a discontinued Android 5.1 smartphone released in June 2016. It features a large 6.44-inch IPS LCD display (1280 x 1920), a Mediatek MT6753 octa-core processor, 3GB of RAM, and storage options of 32GB or 64GB. Notable highlights include a massive 6000 mAh battery, a 13MP main camera, and Dual SIM support.

The VK Mobile VK4000 is a discontinued GSM feature phone announced in March 2006. It is a compact, lightweight device (79g) featuring a 1.8-inch TFT display, 128MB of internal memory, and a basic VGA camera. Key capabilities include Bluetooth, Java support, and an MP3/AAC player, powered by a removable 800mAh Li-Ion battery.

Released in November 2023, the itel A70 is an entry-level smartphone featuring a 6.6-inch IPS LCD display and running Android 13 (Go edition) on a Unisoc T603 octa-core chipset. It offers flexible storage options up to 256GB with 3GB or 4GB of RAM, a 13MP dual main camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and a large 5000mAh battery with 10W wired charging.

The Sendo X is a discontinued GSM phone released in Q4 2003. It features a 2.2-inch TFT display (176x220 pixels), runs on Symbian 6.1 with a 120 MHz ARM925T CPU, and includes 32MB of internal memory with MMC/SD expansion. It is equipped with a VGA main camera with LED flash, Bluetooth 1.1, and an infrared port, powered by a removable 1050 mAh Li-Po battery.

The Realme Narzo 60x, released in September 2023, is a 5G smartphone featuring a 6.72-inch 120Hz IPS LCD display and a Mediatek Dimensity 6100+ chipset. It comes with 128GB storage and 4GB or 6GB of RAM, powered by a 5000mAh battery with 33W fast charging. The device includes a 50MP dual main camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and runs Android 13, priced at ₹12,999.

The LG K92 5G, released in November 2020, is a 5G-enabled smartphone featuring a large 6.7-inch IPS LCD display with 1080 x 2400 resolution. It is powered by a Snapdragon 690 5G chipset with 6GB RAM and 128GB internal storage. Notable hardware includes a 64MP quad-camera system capable of 4K video, a 16MP selfie camera, and a 4000mAh battery with Quick Charge 4.0. Additional features include stereo speakers, a side-mounted fingerprint sensor, and NFC.

The Wind Van Gogh 2100 was a compact GSM phone announced in October 2007 but ultimately cancelled. It featured a 1.8-inch TFT display, a 2MP main camera, 128MB of internal memory with microSD support, and a unique built-in detachable Bluetooth earpiece. It was powered by a removable 820 mAh battery providing up to 3 hours of talk time.

The Spice Smart Flo 358 (Mi-358) is a discontinued entry-level Android 4.4.2 (KitKat) smartphone released in October 2014. It features a compact 3.5-inch TFT display, a dual-core 1.3 GHz CPU, and minimal memory with 256MB RAM and 512MB internal storage. The device includes a 2MP main camera with LED flash, a 1.3MP selfie camera, and is powered by a 1450 mAh Li-Ion battery.

The Motorola Edge (2023) is a 5G smartphone priced at $349.99, featuring a 6.6-inch 144Hz P-OLED display and an IP68 water-resistant build with an eco-leather back. It is powered by a MediaTek Dimensity 7030 chipset with 8GB RAM and 256GB storage. Notable hardware includes a 50MP main camera with OIS, a 32MP selfie camera, and a 4400mAh battery supporting 68W wired and 15W wireless charging.

The Huawei Watch Ultimate Design is a luxury smartwatch released in October 2023, priced at approximately 4,360 EUR. It features a premium build with an 18k gold bezel and crown, sapphire crystal, and a zircon-based alloy case. The device boasts a 1.5-inch LTPO AMOLED display, runs HarmonyOS 4.0, and is highly durable with IP68 and 10 ATM water resistance for diving. Key features include comprehensive health sensors (ECG, SpO2, body temperature), multi-system GPS, and a 530 mAh battery with wireless charging, though it lacks cellular connectivity.

The Plum Optimax 13 is a budget 10.1-inch Android 8.0 (Go edition) tablet released in January 2019. It features a basic 800 x 1280 IPS LCD display, a Spreadtrum SC7731 quad-core processor, and minimal memory with 1GB RAM and 8GB internal storage. It is equipped with a 5MP main camera, a 2MP selfie camera, and a 4700 mAh battery, supporting Dual SIM GSM/HSPA connectivity.

The Innostream INNO 36 was a compact GSM phone announced in Q2 2005 but ultimately cancelled. It featured a dual-display setup (TFT main and STN external), a VGA camera, and basic connectivity via infrared and GPRS, powered by a 920mAh removable Li-Ion battery.

The Toshiba Excite 10 SE is a discontinued 10.1-inch Android 4.1 tablet released in December 2012. It features a 1280x800 IPS LCD display, an Nvidia Tegra 3 quad-core processor, 1GB of RAM, and 16GB of internal storage. Lacking cellular connectivity, it relies on Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 3.0 for communications and includes a 3.15 MP main camera and a 1.2 MP selfie camera.

The Unnecto Neo V is a discontinued Android 5.1 smartphone released in July 2016. It features a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display (480 x 854), a quad-core 1.3 GHz processor, 1GB of RAM, and 8GB of internal storage. It is equipped with an 8MP main camera, a 1.3MP selfie camera, and is powered by a removable 2000 mAh battery.

The Posh Optima LTE L530 is a discontinued Android 5.1 smartphone released in April 2016. It features a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display (720x1280), an octa-core 1.3 GHz Mediatek MT6753 chipset, 2GB of RAM, and 16GB of internal storage. Notably, it is equipped with matching 13MP front and rear cameras and is powered by a non-removable 3000 mAh battery.

The Dell Streak 7 Wi-Fi is a discontinued 7-inch Android tablet released in April 2011. It features a 480x800 TFT display with Gorilla Glass, is powered by an Nvidia Tegra 2 dual-core processor, and includes 16GB of internal storage. Notably, it lacks cellular connectivity, relying on Wi-Fi, and is equipped with a 5MP main camera and a 2780 mAh battery.

The Cubot Note 21, released in September 2023, is an affordable Android 13 smartphone priced around $79.99. It features a 6.56-inch 90Hz IPS LCD display, a Unisoc T606 octa-core processor, 6GB of RAM, and 128GB of internal storage. Notable hardware includes a 50MP dual main camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and a large 5200 mAh battery with 10W wired charging.

The MWg Atom Life is a discontinued Windows Mobile 6 Professional smartphone released in January 2007. It features a 2.7-inch resistive touchscreen, an Intel XScale 624 MHz CPU, 64MB RAM, and 1GB ROM. Notable hardware includes a 2MP main camera with LED flash, a VGA selfie camera, and a removable 1530 mAh battery. Connectivity options include GSM/HSPA, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 1.2, and an infrared port.

Released in 2023, the itel Smart Watch 2 is a basic black wearable featuring a 1.8-inch IPS LCD display and an IP68 rating. It runs on a proprietary OS and includes health sensors for heart rate, SpO2, and acceleration, powered by a 230 mAh battery. The device lacks cellular connectivity, Wi-Fi, and a camera, relying on Bluetooth 5.1 for communication.

The Sony Ericsson WT18i is a discontinued Android-based smartphone released in Q3 2011. It features a compact 3.2-inch TFT display, a 3.15 MP main camera, and is powered by an 806 MHz Marvell PXA 920 CPU with 150MB of internal memory. The device is equipped with a removable 1200 mAh battery, a Walkman player, and supports GSM/TD-SCDMA networks.

The VK Mobile VK7000, announced in March 2006, was a compact GSM/UMTS phone that was ultimately cancelled. It featured a small 1.8-inch TFT display, a 1.3 MP main camera, a VGA front camera for videocalls, and an 800mAh removable Li-Ion battery.

Released in October 2018, the Panasonic Eluga X1 Pro is a premium-build smartphone featuring a stainless steel frame, glass front and back, and a 6.18-inch IPS LCD display (1080 x 2246). It is powered by a Helio P60 chipset with options for 4GB or 6GB of RAM and 64GB or 128GB of storage. Notable features include a 16MP dual rear camera, a 16MP selfie camera, Infrared Face ID, and wireless charging support for its 3000 mAh battery. It runs Android 8.1 and was priced at approximately 350 EUR.

The AT&T Quickfire is a discontinued QWERTY keyboard phone released in November 2008. It features a 2.8-inch TFT display (240x320), a 1.3 MP main camera, and minimal internal memory of 29MB, expandable via microSD. Connectivity is limited to GSM/HSPA and Bluetooth 1.2, lacking WLAN and a 3.5mm jack. It is powered by a removable 1200 mAh battery providing up to 3 hours of talk time.

The Fairphone 4 is a 5G-enabled smartphone released in October 2021, featuring a 6.3-inch IPS LCD display and a Snapdragon 750G 5G chipset. It offers memory configurations of up to 256GB storage and 8GB RAM, a dual 48MP rear camera system with 4K video, and a 25MP selfie camera. Notable for its durability and sustainability, it is MIL-STD-810G compliant with IP54 resistance, includes a removable 3905 mAh battery, and comes with a standard 5-year warranty.

The Apple iPhone 15 Plus, released in September 2023, features a 6.7-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display with a peak brightness of 2000 nits. It is powered by the A16 Bionic chipset with 6GB of RAM and available storage options up to 512GB. The device includes a dual main camera system led by a 48MP wide lens and a 12MP selfie camera, both supporting 4K video. Key hardware features include an IP68 rating, USB Type-C connectivity, and a 4383 mAh battery supporting MagSafe and Qi wireless charging. It is available in five colors and launched at a price of approximately $929.99.

The Alcatel 1L Pro (2021) is an entry-level smartphone released in Q2 2021, priced around 110 EUR. It features a 6.1-inch IPS LCD display (720 x 1560), is powered by a Unisoc SC9863A octa-core chipset with 2GB RAM and 32GB storage, and runs Android 11 (Go edition). Key hardware includes a 13MP dual rear camera, a 5MP selfie camera, a 3000 mAh battery, and a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor.

Released in February 2018, the verykool s5036 Apollo is an entry-level Android 7.0 smartphone featuring a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display and a Mediatek MT6580M quad-core processor. It has limited memory with 8GB internal storage and 1GB RAM, supported by a removable 2000 mAh battery. Notable hardware includes a dual rear camera (8MP + 2MP), a 5MP selfie camera, and a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor.

The BenQ C36 is a discontinued GSM feature phone released in April 2008. It features a compact 2.0-inch TFT display, a 1.3 MP main camera, and a removable 640 mAh battery. Key highlights include dedicated music keys, dual loudspeakers, an MP3 player, and FM radio, though it lacks Bluetooth, WLAN, and a 3.5mm jack.

The Vodafone Smart V8 is a discontinued Android 7.1.1 smartphone released in June 2017. It features a 5.5-inch Full HD IPS LCD display, a Snapdragon 435 octa-core processor, 3GB of RAM, and 32GB of internal storage. For photography, it is equipped with a 16MP main camera and an 8MP selfie camera. Other notable features include a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor, NFC, and a non-removable 3000 mAh battery with 10W charging.

The Acer Iconia Tab 10 A3-A40 is a discontinued 10.1-inch Android 6.0 tablet released in June 2016. It features a 1920 x 1200 IPS LCD display, a Mediatek MT8163A quad-core processor, 2GB of RAM, and storage options ranging from 16GB to 64GB. Key hardware includes a 6100 mAh battery, quad stereo speakers, and a 5MP main camera, though it lacks cellular connectivity and NFC.

The Maxwest Gravity 5 LTE is a discontinued budget Android 5.1 smartphone released in February 2016. It features a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display (720x1280), a Snapdragon 210 quad-core processor, 1GB of RAM, and 8GB of internal storage. It is equipped with an 8MP main camera, a 2MP selfie camera, and a removable 2200 mAh battery.

The TCL Ion X is an entry-level Android smartphone released in January 2023, priced at approximately 100 EUR. It features a 6.0-inch IPS LCD display (720p), a Mediatek Helio G25 octa-core processor, 3GB of RAM, and 32GB of internal storage. It is equipped with a 13MP main camera, a 5MP selfie camera, and a removable 3000 mAh battery with 10W charging.

The Spice Smart Flo 503 (Mi-503) is a discontinued dual-SIM Android 4.4.2 smartphone released in August 2014. It features a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display (480x854 pixels), a dual-core 1.3 GHz CPU, and limited memory with 512MB RAM and 4GB internal storage. The device is equipped with an 8MP main camera, a 2MP selfie camera, and a 2000 mAh battery.

Released in September 2011, the Sony Ericsson Xperia Arc S is a discontinued Android smartphone featuring a 4.2-inch LED-backlit LCD and a lightweight 117g design. It is powered by a 1.4 GHz Snapdragon S2 processor with 512MB RAM and includes an 8MP main camera capable of 720p video. The device is equipped with a removable 1500 mAh battery and supports HSPA connectivity.

Released in November 2023, the Honor 100 is a 5G smartphone featuring a high-brightness 6.7-inch 120Hz OLED display (2600 nits peak) and is powered by the Snapdragon 7 Gen 3 chipset. It offers high-end memory configurations up to 512GB storage and 16GB RAM, paired with a 5000mAh battery supporting rapid 100W wired charging. Camera capabilities include a 50MP main sensor with OIS and a 50MP selfie camera, both capable of 4K video recording. It retails for approximately 320 EUR.

Released in July 2023, the Tecno Pova 5 is an Android 13 smartphone featuring a 6.78-inch 120Hz IPS LCD display and a Mediatek Helio G99 chipset. It offers 8GB of RAM with storage options of 128GB or 256GB, a 50MP main camera, and an 8MP selfie camera. A standout feature is its large 6000 mAh battery with 45W wired fast charging, priced at approximately ₹11,999.

The Sagem my721z is a discontinued GSM 2G phone released in February 2008. It features a 2.2-inch TFT display, a 3.15 MP main camera, and a removable 1000mAh Li-Ion battery providing up to 3 hours of talk time. The compact silver device includes Bluetooth, FM radio, Java support, and a microSD slot, but lacks Wi-Fi, a selfie camera, and a 3.5mm headphone jack.

The BLU G73, released in June 2023, is an affordable Android 13 smartphone priced around 140 EUR. It features a large 6.8-inch 90Hz IPS LCD display, 128GB of storage with 6GB of RAM, and is powered by an octa-core CPU. Key hardware includes a triple rear camera setup led by a 50MP main sensor, a 5000mAh battery with 18W wired charging, and a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor.

Released in April 2017, the BlackBerry Keyone is a QWERTY-keyboard smartphone featuring a 4.5-inch IPS LCD display (1080x1620) and a Snapdragon 625 chipset. It offers memory configurations of 3GB/32GB or 4GB/64GB, a 12MP main camera capable of 4K video, and a 3500 mAh battery with 18W fast charging. It runs Android 7.1 (upgradable to 8.1) and includes a front-mounted fingerprint sensor.

Released in June 2021, the Gionee Smartwatch 7 is a budget-friendly wearable (approx. 50 EUR) featuring a 1.3-inch TFT LCD display, IP67 water resistance, and a lightweight 35g body. It runs on a proprietary OS and includes health sensors for heart rate, SpO2, and acceleration, powered by a 130 mAh battery via Bluetooth 4.0 connectivity.

Released in March 2021, the Coolpad Cool 10A is an entry-level Android 11 smartphone priced at approximately 90 EUR. It features a 6.52-inch IPS LCD display (720x1600), a Unisoc SC9863A octa-core chipset, 2GB of RAM, and 64GB of internal storage. The device is equipped with a 13MP dual rear camera, a 5MP selfie camera, and a 4000mAh battery with 10W wired charging.

Released in December 2022, the Wiko 5G is a HarmonyOS smartphone featuring a 6.78-inch 120Hz IPS LCD display and a Snapdragon 695 5G chipset. It boasts a high-resolution 108MP quad-camera system, 8GB of RAM with up to 256GB of storage, and a 4000mAh battery supporting fast 66W wired charging. Priced around 270 EUR, it is splash-resistant and available in Black or Silver.

The Philips I908 is a discontinued Dual SIM smartphone released in August 2015. It features a 5.0-inch Full HD IPS LCD display, an octa-core 1.7 GHz CPU, 2GB of RAM, and 16GB of internal storage running Android 4.4.2. It is equipped with a 13MP main camera capable of 1080p video, a 5MP selfie camera, and a 3000 mAh Li-Ion battery.

The HP Elite x3 is a discontinued Windows 10 smartphone released in 2016, featuring a high-resolution 5.96-inch AMOLED display and a Snapdragon 820 chipset with 4GB RAM and 64GB storage. Built for durability, it is IP67 water-resistant and MIL-STD-810G compliant, offering a 16MP main camera, Bang & Olufsen stereo speakers, and Microsoft Continuum support. It is powered by a 4150 mAh battery supporting both wired and wireless charging.

The Infinix Smart 8, released in November 2023, is an affordable smartphone priced around 100 EUR. It features a 6.6-inch 90Hz IPS LCD display, is powered by a Unisoc T606 chipset with 8GB RAM and 128GB storage, and runs on Android 13. Key hardware includes a 13MP dual rear camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and a large 5000mAh battery with 10W wired charging.

Released in July 2022, the BLU Studio X5 Max is an entry-level Android 11 (Go edition) smartphone priced at approximately 50 EUR. It features a 5.7-inch IPS LCD display, a quad-core 1.3 GHz CPU, 2GB RAM, and 32GB of internal storage. The device includes a 5MP dual main camera, a 2MP selfie camera, and is powered by a removable 2700 mAh battery.

The Oukitel RT6 is a rugged 10.1-inch Android 13 tablet released in July 2023, distinguished by its extreme durability (IP68/IP69K, MIL-STD-810H) and a massive 20,000 mAh battery with 33W fast charging. It features a Mediatek MT8788 chipset, 8GB RAM, 256GB storage, and 16MP front and rear cameras, weighing 1030g and priced at approximately 350 EUR.

The LeEco Le 2 is a discontinued smartphone released in April 2016, featuring a 5.5-inch IPS LCD display (1080 x 1920) and running Android 6.0. It offers options for either a Mediatek Helio X20 or Qualcomm Snapdragon 652 chipset, paired with 3GB of RAM and 32GB or 64GB of internal storage. Key hardware includes a 16MP main camera capable of 4K video, an 8MP selfie camera, and a 3000 mAh battery with 18W fast charging. Notable features include an infrared port, USB Type-C, and a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor, though it lacks a 3.5mm headphone jack and expandable storage.

The Kyocera Hydro Life is a discontinued rugged smartphone released in August 2014. It features a 4.5-inch IPS LCD display, a Snapdragon 200 quad-core processor, 1.5GB of RAM, and 8GB of internal storage running Android 4.3. Notable for its extreme durability, it is IP57 dust/water resistant and MIL-STD-810G compliant. It includes a 5MP main camera, a 2MP selfie camera, and a removable 2000 mAh battery.

The Icemobile Prime 5.5 is a discontinued Android 4.4.2 (KitKat) smartphone released in August 2014. It features a 5.46-inch IPS LCD display (720x1280), a quad-core 1.3 GHz Cortex-A7 CPU, 1GB of RAM, and 16GB of internal storage. The device is equipped with an 8MP main camera, a 2MP selfie camera, and a removable 2250 mAh battery.

Released in September 2023, the Blackview A96 is an affordable smartphone priced at $161.69. It features a 6.5-inch 120Hz IPS LCD display, a Mediatek Helio G99 chipset, and up to 12GB of RAM with 256GB of UFS 2.2 storage. The device is equipped with a 48MP dual rear camera system capable of 1440p video, a 16MP selfie camera, and a 4380 mAh battery with 18W wired charging. It runs Android 13 and includes NFC and a side-mounted fingerprint sensor.

The Energizer U680S is an entry-level Android 11 smartphone released in Q3 2021, priced at approximately 120 EUR. Its standout feature is a massive 7000 mAh battery, complemented by a large 6.8-inch IPS LCD display (720 x 1640). It is powered by a Unisoc SC9863A octa-core chipset with 2GB RAM and 32GB storage, and features a triple main camera setup led by a 13MP sensor.

The Ericsson A2628 is a discontinued GSM mobile phone released in 2001. It features a monochrome 4-line graphic display, a Mini-SIM slot, and basic functionality including SMS, WAP 1.1, and three built-in games. Lacking a camera, Bluetooth, and Wi-Fi, it relies on a removable NiMH battery (up to 600mAh) providing between 6 to 11 hours of talk time. It was available in four colors: Astral Blue, Pistachio Yellow, Green Pepper, and Celestial Black.

Released in February 2023, the Lava Yuva 2 Pro is an affordable Android 12 smartphone priced at ₹6,620. It features a 6.52-inch IPS LCD display, a Mediatek Helio G37 chipset, 4GB of RAM, and 64GB of internal storage. The device is equipped with a 5000mAh battery with 10W charging, a 13MP triple rear camera system, and a 5MP selfie camera.

Released in September 2021, the Meizu 18s Pro is a high-end 5G smartphone featuring a 6.7-inch Super AMOLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate and QHD+ resolution. It is powered by the Snapdragon 888+ 5G chipset, with memory options up to 12GB RAM and 256GB UFS 3.1 storage. The device boasts a versatile triple main camera system led by a 50MP wide sensor with OIS, 8K video recording, and a 44MP selfie camera. It is equipped with a 4500 mAh battery supporting 40W wired and wireless charging, and includes premium features like an ultrasonic under-display fingerprint sensor and Gorilla Glass 6 protection.

The Spice Smart Flo 508 (Mi-508) is a discontinued entry-level Android 4.4.2 smartphone released in August 2014. It features a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display (480x854 pixels), a dual-core 1.3 GHz CPU, and limited memory with 512MB RAM and 4GB internal storage. The device includes an 8MP main camera, a 2MP selfie camera, and is powered by a 2000 mAh Li-Ion battery.

The VK Mobile VK300 is a discontinued GSM feature phone announced in July 2005. It is a compact device weighing 75g, featuring a 1.8-inch TFT display and a secondary external STN screen. It lacks a camera, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and a memory card slot, offering basic functionality like SMS/MMS and WAP 1.2.1 browsing. It is powered by a removable 720 mAh Li-Ion battery providing up to 3 hours of talk time.
